analysis.study_scope: Baking metallic, color, roughness, and normal maps, managing margins, saving textures, and assembling baked PBR material sets.

episodes.problem: Baking metallic mask textures efficiently using emission preview workflows.
episodes.observed_fact: Viewer node acts as an Emission shader when previewing node branches in Cycles baking.
episodes.instructor_claim: Bake Type set to Emission bakes whichever grayscale output is currently active on the Viewer node.
episodes.interpretation: Emission baking bypasses lighting calculation to extract raw grayscale data maps directly.
episodes.hypothesis: Any black-and-white mask map can be extracted rapidly using Emission bake mode.
episodes.reference_evidence: Viewer node connected to Material Output surface socket; Bake Type set to Emission.
episodes.modeling_decision: Connect the metallic mask Color Ramp to the Viewer node and bake using Emission mode.
episodes.visible_action: Ctrl+Shift+Click Color Ramp node to connect it to Viewer node; set Bake Type to Emission.
episodes.spoken_reason: Viewer node acts as an emission shader, allowing exact value previews to bake into image textures.
episodes.topology_surface_effect: Outputs grayscale map reflecting metallic values across object UV layout.
episodes.alternatives: Baking metallic via Diffuse mode with lighting disabled.
episodes.transferable_principle: Use Emission bake mode paired with Viewer node previews to extract isolated procedural masks.

episodes.problem: Baking constant uniform metallic values without texture masks.
episodes.observed_fact: Uniform scalar inputs lack node outputs to feed directly into the Viewer node.
episodes.instructor_claim: Adding an RGB node plugged into the Viewer node allows baking single constant colors or values.
episodes.interpretation: RGB nodes supply explicit color vectors required by emission bake workflows.
episodes.hypothesis: Unconnected constant values cannot bake reliably via emission without dedicated input nodes.
episodes.reference_evidence: RGB node added in Shader Editor and set to solid white.
episodes.modeling_decision: Use an RGB color node to represent full or partial uniform metallic values for baking.
episodes.visible_action: Add RGB node via Search, set color to white, and connect to Viewer node.
episodes.spoken_reason: Provides a explicit color signal for the Viewer node to bake uniform material properties.
episodes.topology_surface_effect: Generates solid white or black map corresponding to constant value setting.
episodes.alternatives: Creating constant solid color images directly in Image Editor without baking.
episodes.transferable_principle: Convert uniform scalar material parameters into explicit RGB nodes for emission baking.

episodes.problem: Preventing color space conversion distortion on non-color data bakes.
episodes.observed_fact: Leaving target texture nodes on default sRGB skews non-color data values.
episodes.instructor_claim: Non-color maps like metallic and roughness require target texture Color Space set to Non-Color before baking.
episodes.interpretation: sRGB gamma curves distort linear numerical values intended for non-color shader inputs.
episodes.hypothesis: Incorrect viewer node strength alters baked brightness values non-linearly.
episodes.reference_evidence: Viewer node Strength set to 1.0; Image Texture Color Space changed to Non-Color; Bake button clicked.
episodes.modeling_decision: Verify Viewer strength is 1.0, set target texture to Non-Color, save file, and trigger bake.
episodes.visible_action: Set Viewer Strength to 1.0, set Image Texture to Non-Color, save project, click Bake.
episodes.spoken_reason: Ensures accurate linear value output without gamma curves altering non-color map data.
episodes.topology_surface_effect: Metallic map bakes with correct linear value fidelity across UV islands.
episodes.alternatives: Applying inverse gamma adjustments post-bake in external image editing applications.
episodes.transferable_principle: Set target image nodes to Non-Color before baking non-color data to preserve linear accuracy.

episodes.problem: Controlling pixel padding width at UV island borders during baking.
episodes.observed_fact: Bake settings include a Margin parameter controlling pixel extension beyond UV edges.
episodes.instructor_claim: Margin settings extend boundary pixels to prevent seam artifacts during rendering.
episodes.interpretation: Dilating border pixels prevents background bleeding when mipmapping or filtering textures.
episodes.hypothesis: Smaller bake margins allow tighter UV packing when texture space is limited.
episodes.reference_evidence: Bake panel Margin set to 16px, then adjusted down to 8px and re-baked.
episodes.modeling_decision: Reduce Margin parameter from 16px to 8px to narrow padding borders.
episodes.visible_action: Change Margin value in Bake panel to 8px, re-select target nodes, and click Bake.
episodes.spoken_reason: Customizes dilation padding according to mesh UV density requirements.
episodes.topology_surface_effect: Narrows pixel extension width outside UV island boundaries.
episodes.alternatives: Using high margin values (32px+) for low-LOD distant mesh objects.
episodes.transferable_principle: Adjust bake margin padding to balance seam bleed prevention with UV packing density.

episodes.problem: Preventing loss of baked image buffer data upon closing Blender.
episodes.observed_fact: Newly baked image buffers remain unsaved in temporary memory until manually exported.
episodes.instructor_claim: Blender does not auto-save baked image textures to disk; unsaved bakes are lost on exit.
episodes.interpretation: Image buffers exist strictly in RAM until saved externally to disk storage.
episodes.hypothesis: Unsaved internal image packed data can be lost during scene cleanup or crash recovery.
episodes.reference_evidence: Image > Save As executed in UV Editor; format set to JPEG at 100% quality.
episodes.modeling_decision: Save baked image externally using JPEG format with explicit descriptor naming.
episodes.visible_action: Select Image > Save As, name file 'Dirty Metal Metallic.jpg', set quality to 100%, click Save As Image.
episodes.spoken_reason: Permanently writes baked texture buffer to storage and reduces file footprint.
episodes.topology_surface_effect: Writes metallic map file to local disk storage.
episodes.alternatives: Saving as 16-bit PNG or EXR files for uncompressed raw data retention.
episodes.transferable_principle: Save baked image buffers to external disk files immediately post-bake to avoid data loss.

episodes.problem: Baking clean base color maps without baking scene lighting or metallic artifacts.
episodes.observed_fact: Diffuse bake type includes Direct/Indirect lighting contributions by default and turns black on metallic areas.
episodes.instructor_claim: Disabling Direct and Indirect contributions isolates raw surface color, while metallic value must be 0.
episodes.interpretation: Unchecking light contributions yields unlit albedo color maps suitable for PBR pipelines.
episodes.hypothesis: Leaving metallic values above zero creates black patches in diffuse color bakes.
episodes.reference_evidence: Bake Type set to Diffuse; Direct and Indirect unchecked; Metallic set to 0.0; Color Space set to sRGB.
episodes.modeling_decision: Set Bake Type to Diffuse, uncheck Direct/Indirect light, set Metallic to 0.0, set sRGB, and bake.
episodes.visible_action: Adjust Diffuse bake settings, set Metallic socket to 0.0, ensure sRGB space, click Bake, and save image.
episodes.spoken_reason: Prevents environmental light and shadow from burning permanently into surface color maps.
episodes.topology_surface_effect: Produces unlit albedo base color map across object surface.
episodes.correction: Ensure Metallic setting is lowered to zero prior to diffuse color baking.
episodes.alternatives: Baking base color through an Emission shader workflow.
episodes.transferable_principle: Isolate base color maps by turning off light contributions and metallic values during diffuse baking.

episodes.problem: Baking linear surface roughness maps from procedural material nodes.
episodes.observed_fact: Bake Type menu contains a dedicated Roughness option.
episodes.instructor_claim: Roughness bake mode extracts grayscale values driving the BSDF Roughness input socket.
episodes.interpretation: Dedicated bake modes automatically isolate specific BSDF channel inputs.
episodes.hypothesis: Target image nodes must use Non-Color color space to preserve linear roughness values.
episodes.reference_evidence: Bake Type set to Roughness; target node set to Non-Color; baked grayscale image saved.
episodes.modeling_decision: Select Roughness bake mode, set target image to Non-Color, execute bake, and save file.
episodes.visible_action: Select Roughness in Bake Type, set Color Space to Non-Color, click Bake, save as 'Dirty Metal Roughness.jpg'.
episodes.spoken_reason: Captures micro-surface glossiness data linearly without color space distortion.
episodes.topology_surface_effect: Generates baked linear roughness map for surface reflection control.
episodes.alternatives: Baking roughness map via Viewer node and Emission bake type.
episodes.transferable_principle: Use native Roughness bake mode with Non-Color color space to capture linear roughness maps.

episodes.problem: Baking procedural height and bump nodes into a tangent-space normal map.
episodes.observed_fact: Bump node network feeds height data into Principled BSDF Normal input.
episodes.instructor_claim: Normal bake mode converts procedural height/bump inputs into standard tangent-space normal maps.
episodes.interpretation: Translates surface vector gradients into RGB-encoded directional normal vectors.
episodes.hypothesis: Normal map baking requires Non-Color color space settings on target texture nodes.
episodes.reference_evidence: Bake Type set to Normal; target node set to Non-Color; purple tangent-space map produced.
episodes.modeling_decision: Select Normal bake type, ensure Non-Color space, click Bake, and save image file.
episodes.visible_action: Set Bake Type to Normal, confirm Non-Color color space, click Bake, save image as 'Dirty Metal Normal.jpg'.
episodes.spoken_reason: Bakes vector surface orientation data needed for low-poly shading details.
episodes.topology_surface_effect: Produces tangent-space normal map displaying characteristic purple-blue vector hues.
episodes.alternatives: Baking object-space or world-space normal maps for specialized game engines.
episodes.transferable_principle: Convert procedural bump networks into tangent-space normal maps using Normal bake mode and Non-Color color space.

episodes.problem: Assembling baked PBR map files into a clean non-procedural material setup.
episodes.observed_fact: Node Wrangler's Ctrl+Shift+T shortcut auto-connects texture maps based on file suffix keywords.
episodes.instructor_claim: Node Wrangler parses map names to wire Base Color, Metallic, Roughness, and Normal maps automatically.
episodes.interpretation: Standardized file suffixes enable automated node graph assembly for PBR textures.
episodes.hypothesis: Incorrect texture file naming causes misassigned texture sockets during auto-import.
episodes.reference_evidence: Fake User set on source material; new material created; Ctrl+Shift+T pressed; PBR set loaded.
episodes.modeling_decision: Enable Fake User on original procedural material, create new material, auto-import baked textures via Node Wrangler.
episodes.visible_action: Enable Fake User shield icon, create new material, press Ctrl+Shift+T, select baked texture set, manually correct misassigned Metallic map.
episodes.spoken_reason: Protects source procedural material tree while setting up lightweight baked PBR textures.
episodes.topology_surface_effect: Replaces complex procedural shader node graph with optimized image-based PBR material.
episodes.failure: Node Wrangler auto-assigned 'Dirty Metal Normal' into the Metallic texture slot.
episodes.correction: Manually selected 'Dirty Metal Metallic' file in texture node and reset Color Space to Non-Color.
episodes.alternatives: Manually adding and wiring individual Image Texture nodes into Principled BSDF inputs.
episodes.transferable_principle: Protect source procedural graphs with Fake User and use standardized file names for auto-building PBR material sets.
